cvs: 'Adolphe Audusson' – blood-red semi-double, earlier · 'Bob Hope' – very dark red · 'Nobilissima' – white peony form, very early · 'Elegans' – pink anemone form
foliage: evergreen; glossy, leathery dark green oval leaves
hardinessNote: Hardy in most places throughout the UK, even in a cold winter, approximately -15 to -10°C; frost can brown open flowers.
pollination: not applicable; grown for flowers, not fruit
prune: Little needed. Shape lightly straight after flowering, before new buds set.
resilience: Tough, long-lived evergreen in shade. Avoid east facings, where early sun on frosted flowers browns them. Pests: scale insects, vine weevil, occasional aphids.
soilWarning: Lime or chalk causes yellow leaves
uncertain: colour: described as deep red, crimson or salmon-red depending on source
peak: sources give March to May; Pleasant Run says from April
height: RHS 2.5–4 m; some UK sellers 1.5–2 m
uses: Shady borders · woodland gardens · containers · north or west walls · winter structure
visual: Large semi-double to double salmon-red flowers in spring · glossy dark evergreen leaves
water: Water regularly, especially July to September while buds form; use rainwater in pots. Dry spells cause bud drop.
